metadata.title: ASVAB Study Bank
metadata.description: ASVAB practice question bank covering all 10 subtests for Space Force Officer candidate preparation.

questions.question: A car travels 240 miles on 8 gallons of gas. What is its fuel efficiency in miles per gallon?
questions.explanation: Divide total miles by total gallons. 240 / 8 = 30 mpg.

questions.question: If 3 pencils cost $0.45, how much would 8 pencils cost at the same rate?
A shirt is on sale for 25 percent off its original price of $40. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: 25 percent of 40 is 10. The sale price is 40 minus 10, which equals $30.

questions.question: A worker earns $15 per hour and works 32 hours in a week. What is the gross pay?
questions.explanation: Multiply hourly rate by hours worked. 15 x 32 = $480.

questions.question: A recipe uses 2 cups of flour to make 12 cookies. How much flour is needed for 30 cookies?
questions.explanation: Set up the ratio 2/12 = x/30. Cross multiply to get 12x = 60, so x = 5 cups.

questions.question: The sum of three consecutive integers is 78. What is the smallest of the three integers?
questions.explanation: Average is 78 / 3 = 26, which is the middle integer. The integers are 25, 26, 27, so the smallest is 25.

questions.question: If 40 percent of a number is 60, what is the number?
questions.explanation: Divide the part by the percent in decimal form. 60 / 0.40 = 150.

questions.question: Two trains start 300 miles apart and travel toward each other. One travels at 50 mph and the other at 70 mph. How long until they meet?
questions.explanation: Combined closing speed is 50 + 70 = 120 mph. Time equals distance divided by speed. 300 / 120 = 2.5 hours.

questions.question: A pizza costs $12.00 plus 8 percent sales tax. What is the total cost?
If you save $50 per week, how much will you save in one year (52 weeks)?
questions.explanation: Multiply weekly savings by number of weeks. 50 x 52 = $2,600.

questions.question: A 60 foot rope is cut into three pieces in the ratio 2:3:5. How long is the longest piece?
questions.explanation: The ratio sums to 10 parts. Each part is 60 / 10 = 6 feet. The longest piece equals 5 parts, or 5 x 6 = 30 feet.

questions.question: If 15 workers can complete a job in 8 days, how long would it take 10 workers to do the same job?
questions.explanation: Total work is 15 x 8 = 120 worker days. With 10 workers, 120 / 10 = 12 days.

questions.question: A car uses 1 gallon of gas every 25 miles. How many gallons are needed for a 350 mile trip?
questions.explanation: Divide distance by miles per gallon. 350 / 25 = 14 gallons.

questions.question: A $200 jacket is marked up 30 percent, then discounted 20 percent. What is the final price?
questions.explanation: After markup: 200 x 1.30 = 260. After discount: 260 x 0.80 = $208.

questions.question: The average of 5 numbers is 14. What is their sum?
questions.explanation: Sum equals average times count. 14 x 5 = 70.

questions.question: A class of 24 students has a girl to boy ratio of 5:3. How many girls are in the class?
questions.explanation: Total ratio parts equal 5 + 3 = 8. Each part equals 24 / 8 = 3 students. Girls equal 5 x 3 = 15.

questions.question: A man invests $5,000 at 6 percent simple interest for 3 years. How much interest is earned?
questions.explanation: Simple interest formula: I = P x r x t. 5000 x 0.06 x 3 = $900.

questions.question: If 12 oranges cost $3.60, what is the cost of 18 oranges at the same rate?
A worker's salary rises from $40,000 to $44,000. What is the percent increase?
questions.explanation: Increase is 4,000. Percent equals 4000 / 40000 = 0.10 or 10 percent.

questions.question: A 30 percent acid solution has a volume of 200 mL. How much pure water must be added to make a 20 percent solution?
questions.explanation: Acid amount is fixed at 200 x 0.30 = 60 mL. Set 60 / (200 + x) = 0.20. Solve: 200 + x = 300, x = 100 mL.

questions.question: A 500 gallon water tank leaks at 5 gallons per hour. How long until it is empty?
questions.explanation: Divide total volume by leak rate. 500 / 5 = 100 hours.

questions.question: A car bought for $20,000 depreciates 10 percent each year. What is its value after 2 years?
questions.explanation: Apply 0.90 multiplier each year. 20000 x 0.9 = 18000. Then 18000 x 0.9 = $16,200.

questions.question: A rectangular field is 12 meters long and 8 meters wide. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of rectangle equals length times width. 12 x 8 = 96 square meters.

questions.question: A box of cereal weighs 16 ounces. How many ounces are in a case of 12 boxes?
questions.explanation: Multiply weight per box by number of boxes. 16 x 12 = 192 ounces.

questions.question: John leaves at 9 AM driving 60 mph. Sarah leaves at 10 AM from the same starting point driving 80 mph in the same direction. At what time does Sarah catch up to John?
questions.explanation: At 10 AM, John is 60 miles ahead. Sarah closes the gap at 80 minus 60, or 20 mph. 60 / 20 = 3 hours. 10 AM plus 3 hours equals 1 PM.

questions.question: Solve for x: 3x + 7 = 22
questions.explanation: Subtract 7 from both sides to get 3x = 15. Divide by 3 to get x = 5.

questions.question: Factor the expression x squared minus 9.
questions.explanation: This is a difference of squares: a squared minus b squared equals (a - b)(a + b). Here a = x and b = 3.

questions.question: Simplify: (2x squared)(3x cubed)
questions.explanation: Multiply coefficients: 2 x 3 = 6. Add exponents on the same base: 2 + 3 = 5. Result is 6x to the 5th power.

questions.question: What is the slope of the line passing through (2, 3) and (5, 9)?
What is the area of a circle with radius 5?
questions.explanation: Area equals pi times radius squared. pi x 5 squared = 25 pi.

questions.question: A right triangle has legs of length 6 and 8. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: Use the Pythagorean theorem: a squared plus b squared equals c squared. 36 + 64 = 100, so c equals the square root of 100, which is 10.

questions.question: What is the square root of 144?
questions.explanation: 12 multiplied by 12 equals 144, so the square root of 144 is 12.

questions.question: Expand (x + 3) squared.
questions.explanation: (x + 3)(x + 3) equals x squared + 3x + 3x + 9, which simplifies to x squared + 6x + 9.

questions.question: Solve for x: 2x - 5 = 3x + 1
questions.explanation: Subtract 2x from both sides: -5 = x + 1. Subtract 1 to get x = -6.

questions.question: What is the volume of a cube with side length 4?
questions.explanation: Volume of a cube equals side cubed. 4 x 4 x 4 = 64.

questions.question: If f(x) = 2x + 3, what is f(4)?
questions.explanation: Substitute x = 4 into the function. 2(4) + 3 = 8 + 3 = 11.

questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of a triangle?
questions.explanation: By definition in Euclidean geometry, the interior angles of any triangle sum to 180 degrees.

questions.question: Solve x squared equals 49.
questions.explanation: Both 7 squared and (-7) squared equal 49, so the equation has two solutions.

questions.question: Solve the quadratic x squared minus 5x plus 6 equals 0.
questions.explanation: Factor as (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0. Solutions are x = 2 and x = 3.

questions.question: What is the surface area of a cube with side length 3?
questions.explanation: Surface area equals 6 times side squared. 6 x 9 = 54.

questions.question: What is 5 factorial?
questions.explanation: 5! equals 5 x 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 120.

questions.question: Simplify (x squared) cubed.
questions.explanation: When raising a power to a power, multiply the exponents. 2 x 3 = 6.

questions.question: If 2 to the x equals 32, what is x?
questions.explanation: 2 to the 5th equals 32, so x equals 5.

questions.question: What is the perimeter of a rectangle that is 5 units by 8 units?
questions.explanation: Perimeter equals 2 times length plus 2 times width. 2(5) + 2(8) = 10 + 16 = 26.

questions.question: What is the median of the set {3, 7, 9, 11, 15}?
questions.explanation: The set is already in order. The middle value of five elements is the third one, which is 9.

questions.question: What is the slope of a horizontal line?
questions.explanation: A horizontal line has no rise, so the slope (rise over run) is 0.

questions.question: Multiply (3x + 2)(x - 5).
questions.explanation: Use FOIL: 3x squared - 15x + 2x - 10. Combine like terms: 3x squared - 13x - 10.

questions.question: What is the value of log base 10 of 1000?
questions.explanation: 10 to the 3rd power equals 1000, so log base 10 of 1000 equals 3.

questions.question: What is the value of sin(30 degrees)?
questions.explanation: From standard trigonometric values, sin(30 degrees) equals 1/2 or 0.5.

questions.question: If a circle has a diameter of 10, what is its circumference?
questions.explanation: Circumference equals pi times diameter. pi x 10 = 10 pi.

questions.question: Using Ohm's Law, what is the voltage across a 10 ohm resistor with 2 amps of current flowing through it?
questions.explanation: Ohm's Law states V = I times R. 2 amps x 10 ohms = 20 volts.

questions.question: What is the unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms, symbolized by the Greek letter omega.

questions.question: What is the unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: Current is the flow of charge per unit time, measured in amperes (amps).

questions.question: In a series circuit with three resistors of 2, 3, and 5 ohms, what is the total resistance?
questions.explanation: In a series circuit, total resistance equals the sum of all resistances. 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 ohms.

questions.question: Two 6 ohm resistors are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
questions.explanation: For two equal resistors in parallel, total resistance equals one half of one resistor. 6 / 2 = 3 ohms.

questions.question: What is the unit of capacitance?
questions.explanation: Capacitance, the ability of a component to store electric charge, is measured in farads.

questions.question: What is the unit of inductance?
questions.explanation: Inductance, the property of a coil to oppose changes in current, is measured in henries.

questions.question: What is the unit of frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency, the number of cycles per second, is measured in hertz (Hz).

questions.question: What is the power dissipated by a device operating at 12 volts and drawing 2 amps?
questions.explanation: Power equals voltage times current. P = V x I = 12 x 2 = 24 watts.

questions.question: What does AC stand for in electronics?
questions.explanation: AC stands for Alternating Current, which periodically reverses direction. DC, by contrast, flows in one direction.

questions.question: What does DC stand for?
questions.explanation: DC stands for Direct Current, which flows steadily in one direction. Batteries provide DC.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a diode?
options: Allow current in only one direction
questions.answer: Allow current in only one direction
questions.explanation: A diode acts as a one way valve for current. It permits flow in the forward direction and blocks reverse flow.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a transistor?
questions.explanation: Transistors are semiconductor devices used to amplify signals or act as electronic switches in circuits.

questions.question: Power can be calculated using P = I squared times R. If I = 3 amps and R = 4 ohms, what is the power?
questions.explanation: P = I squared x R = 9 x 4 = 36 watts.

questions.question: What is the standard household voltage in the United States?
questions.explanation: Standard residential outlets in the US deliver about 120 volts AC at 60 Hz.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best electrical insulator?
questions.explanation: Rubber resists the flow of electricity, making it an insulator. Copper and aluminum are conductors.

questions.question: Which material is the best electrical conductor among the following?
questions.explanation: Copper has very low resistivity and is the most common conductor used in wiring. Glass and plastic are insulators.

questions.question: Silicon and germanium are examples of what?
questions.explanation: Silicon and germanium have conductivity between that of conductors and insulators. They form the basis of most modern electronics.

questions.question: What is the standard AC frequency in the United States?
questions.explanation: The US power grid runs at 60 Hz. Most of Europe and parts of Asia use 50 Hz.

questions.question: When batteries are connected in series, what happens?
questions.explanation: Series connection sums the individual voltages. Two 1.5 volt batteries in series produce 3 volts.

questions.question: When batteries are connected in parallel, what is the main effect?
questions.explanation: Parallel connection keeps voltage constant but adds the capacities, allowing the circuit to source current for longer.

questions.question: What does a transformer do?
questions.explanation: Transformers use electromagnetic induction to change AC voltage levels. They do not change the frequency.

questions.question: In the resistor color code, what value does the color red represent?
questions.explanation: Standard resistor color codes assign black=0, brown=1, red=2, orange=3, yellow=4, green=5, blue=6, violet=7, gray=8, white=9.

questions.question: What happens to total resistance in a parallel circuit when more resistors are added?
questions.explanation: Adding parallel paths gives current more routes. Total resistance is always less than the smallest individual resistor in the parallel branch.

questions.question: What is the symbol used for ground in circuit diagrams?
options: Three horizontal lines decreasing in size
questions.answer: Three horizontal lines decreasing in size
questions.explanation: Earth ground is typically represented by a stack of three horizontal lines that get progressively shorter.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.explanation: Water is composed of two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom, written as H2O.

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is a gas giant with a mass more than twice that of all other planets combined.

questions.question: What is the approximate speed of light in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: Light travels at roughly 3 x 10 to the 8th meters per second, equivalent to 300,000 kilometers per second.

questions.question: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP through cellular respiration, supplying most of the energy used by the cell.

questions.question: What does DNA stand for?
questions.explanation: DNA stands for Deoxyribonucleic Acid. It carries genetic information in nearly all living organisms.

questions.question: What pH value is considered neutral?
questions.explanation: On the pH scale of 0 to 14, a value of 7 is neutral. Below 7 is acidic, and above 7 is basic.

questions.question: An atom's atomic number equals the number of which subatomic particle?
questions.explanation: The atomic number defines the element and equals the number of protons in the nucleus of the atom.

questions.question: At sea level, what is the boiling point of water in Celsius?
questions.explanation: Pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius (212 degrees Fahrenheit) at standard atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: What is the freezing point of water in Fahrenheit?
questions.explanation: Water freezes at 32 degrees Fahrenheit, which corresponds to 0 degrees Celsius.

questions.question: What element has the chemical symbol Au?
questions.explanation: Au is from the Latin word aurum, which means gold.

questions.question: What element has the chemical symbol Fe?
questions.explanation: Fe is derived from the Latin word ferrum, which means iron.

questions.question: What is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Earth's atmosphere is roughly 78 percent nitrogen, 21 percent oxygen, and 1 percent other gases.

questions.question: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: The skin is the largest organ by surface area and weight in the human body.

questions.question: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.explanation: Adults have 206 bones. Infants are born with about 270, but many fuse during growth.

questions.question: What is the approximate speed of sound in air at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Sound travels at roughly 343 meters per second in dry air at 20 degrees Celsius.

questions.question: What is the acceleration due to gravity near Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: Free fall acceleration near Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 meters per second squared.

questions.question: What is the hardest naturally occurring substance?
questions.explanation: Diamond ranks 10 on the Mohs hardness scale, the highest natural rating.

questions.question: What is the electrical charge of an electron?
questions.explanation: Electrons carry a negative elementary charge, opposite that of protons.

questions.question: Which formula represents Newton's second law of motion?
questions.explanation: Newton's second law states that force equals mass multiplied by acceleration.

questions.question: What gas do plants release during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide and water and use sunlight to produce glucose. Oxygen is released as a byproduct.

questions.question: What is the Earth's outer core primarily composed of?
questions.explanation: The outer core is a liquid layer of mostly iron and nickel. Convection there generates Earth's magnetic field.

questions.question: How many chromosomes are in a typical human body cell?
questions.explanation: Human somatic cells contain 23 pairs of chromosomes for a total of 46. Sex cells (gametes) contain only 23.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars appears red due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface.

questions.question: Which scientist proposed the three laws of motion?
questions.explanation: Sir Isaac Newton formulated the three classical laws of motion in his 1687 work Principia Mathematica.

questions.question: What is the basic unit of life?
questions.explanation: All known living organisms are composed of one or more cells, the smallest unit considered alive.

questions.question: A car rents for $50 per day plus $0.20 per mile. What is the total for a 3 day rental with 100 miles driven?
questions.explanation: Daily charge is 50 x 3 = 150. Mileage is 100 x 0.20 = 20. Total is 150 + 20 = 170.

questions.question: A school has 600 students and 60 percent are girls. How many boys attend?
questions.explanation: If 60 percent are girls then 40 percent are boys. 600 x 0.40 = 240 boys.

questions.question: Four pumps fill a tank in 5 hours. How long would 5 pumps of equal capacity take?
questions.explanation: Total work is 4 x 5 = 20 pump hours. With 5 pumps, time equals 20 / 5 = 4 hours.

questions.question: A train covers 240 miles in 4 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Speed equals distance divided by time. 240 / 4 = 60 mph.

questions.question: Mary has three times as many marbles as John. Together they have 48 marbles. How many does Mary have?
questions.explanation: Let John have x marbles. Then Mary has 3x. Together x + 3x = 4x = 48, so x = 12 and Mary has 36.

questions.question: A train travels 60 mph for 4 hours, then 80 mph for 2 hours. What total distance is covered?
questions.explanation: Distance equals rate times time. 60 x 4 = 240. 80 x 2 = 160. Sum is 240 + 160 = 400 miles.

questions.question: What is a 15 percent tip on a $60 meal?
questions.explanation: 15 percent of 60 equals 0.15 x 60 = 9. The tip is $9.

questions.question: An item with an original price of $50 is marked 30 percent off, then an additional 20 percent off the discounted price. What is the final price?
questions.explanation: After first discount: 50 x 0.70 = 35. After second discount: 35 x 0.80 = 28.

questions.question: If 5 apples cost $2.00, how much do 12 apples cost at the same rate?
A worker assembles 8 widgets per hour. How many can be assembled in 6.5 hours?
questions.explanation: Multiply rate by time. 8 x 6.5 = 52 widgets.

questions.question: A class has a teacher to student ratio of 1 to 15. There are 30 students. How many teachers are there?
questions.explanation: Divide students by ratio. 30 / 15 = 2 teachers.

questions.question: A solution is 60 percent sugar by mass. How much sugar is in 250 grams of solution?
questions.explanation: Multiply total mass by percentage. 250 x 0.60 = 150 g.

questions.question: Sara is twice as old as Tom. In 5 years, the sum of their ages will be 28. How old is Sara now?
questions.explanation: Let Tom be t now. Sara is 2t. In 5 years: (2t + 5) + (t + 5) = 28. So 3t + 10 = 28 and t = 6. Sara is 12.

questions.question: A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Side length equals 36 / 4 = 9. Area equals side squared: 9 x 9 = 81 square cm.

questions.question: A box has 24 chocolates and 3/8 of them are dark. How many are dark?
questions.explanation: Multiply total by the fraction. 24 x 3 / 8 = 72 / 8 = 9.

questions.question: A buyer purchases 12 items at $3.50 each. What is the total cost?
questions.explanation: Multiply count by unit price. 12 x 3.50 = $42.00.

questions.question: A company has 200 employees. 25 percent work in sales and 30 percent in engineering. How many work in neither department?
questions.explanation: Sales plus engineering equals 25 + 30 = 55 percent. Remaining is 45 percent. 200 x 0.45 = 90.

questions.question: If 8 widgets cost $24, what would 30 widgets cost?
questions.explanation: Unit price is 24 / 8 = $3. Then 30 x 3 = $90.

questions.question: An $18,000 car depreciates 15 percent in one year. What is its value after that year?
questions.explanation: Apply 0.85 multiplier. 18000 x 0.85 = $15,300.

questions.question: Three friends split a $90 dinner equally. How much does each pay?
questions.explanation: Divide total by number of payers. 90 / 3 = $30.

questions.question: A rectangle has an area of 60 square units and a width of 5 units. What is the length?
questions.explanation: Length equals area divided by width. 60 / 5 = 12 units.

questions.question: A 25 ft pole casts a 10 ft shadow. A nearby tree casts a 24 ft shadow at the same time. How tall is the tree?
questions.explanation: Set up the proportion. Tree height / 24 = 25 / 10. Cross multiply: tree height = (25 x 24) / 10 = 60 ft.

questions.question: If 80 percent of a class of 30 students passed a test, how many passed?
questions.explanation: Multiply class size by passing percentage. 30 x 0.80 = 24 students.

questions.question: A factory produces 240 units in 8 hours. At the same rate, how many units would be produced in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: Rate is 240 / 8 = 30 units per hour. Then 30 x 12 = 360.

questions.question: What is 3/4 of 80?
questions.explanation: Multiply the fraction by the whole. 80 x 3 / 4 = 240 / 4 = 60.

questions.question: Solve for x: 4(x - 3) = 12
questions.explanation: Distribute or divide: x - 3 = 3. Add 3 to both sides: x = 6.

questions.question: Simplify a to the 4th times a cubed.
questions.explanation: When multiplying like bases, add the exponents. 4 + 3 = 7.

questions.question: Simplify x to the 5th divided by x squared.
questions.explanation: When dividing like bases, subtract the exponents. 5 - 2 = 3.

questions.question: Find the distance between the points (0, 0) and (3, 4).
questions.explanation: Distance equals the square root of (3 squared plus 4 squared) = square root of 25 = 5.

questions.question: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 and height 6?
questions.explanation: Area equals one half times base times height. 0.5 x 10 x 6 = 30.

questions.question: What is the volume of a cylinder with radius 2 and height 5?
questions.explanation: Volume equals pi r squared h. pi x 4 x 5 = 20 pi.

questions.question: Solve: x divided by 4 equals 6.
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by 4: x = 24.

questions.question: Rewrite x to the negative 2 power with a positive exponent.
questions.explanation: A negative exponent means take the reciprocal. x to the negative 2 equals 1 over x squared.

questions.question: Multiply: (5x)(2x).
questions.explanation: Multiply coefficients (5 x 2 = 10) and add exponents on the same base (1 + 1 = 2).

questions.question: What is 3 factorial plus 4 factorial?
questions.explanation: 3! equals 6 and 4! equals 24. 6 + 24 = 30.

questions.question: What is the value of cos(60 degrees)?
questions.explanation: From standard trig values, cos(60 degrees) equals 1/2 or 0.5.

questions.question: What is the value of tan(45 degrees)?
questions.explanation: Tan(45 degrees) equals sin(45) / cos(45) = (sqrt(2)/2) / (sqrt(2)/2) = 1.

questions.question: Factor: x squared plus 5x plus 6.
questions.explanation: Find two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 5: 2 and 3. So the factors are (x + 2)(x + 3).

questions.question: What is the midpoint of the segment connecting (2, 4) and (8, 10)?
questions.explanation: Midpoint formula: average each coordinate. ((2 + 8) / 2, (4 + 10) / 2) = (5, 7).

questions.question: Solve: |x - 3| = 5.
questions.explanation: Absolute value equation splits into two: x - 3 = 5 gives x = 8, and x - 3 = -5 gives x = -2.

questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral?
questions.explanation: For an n sided polygon, interior angles sum to (n - 2) x 180 degrees. For n = 4 that is 360 degrees.

questions.question: If the radius of a circle is doubled, by what factor does the area increase?
questions.explanation: Area is proportional to radius squared. Doubling the radius multiplies the area by 2 squared, which is 4.

questions.question: Solve: x squared minus 4 = 0.
questions.explanation: Add 4 then take the square root of both sides. Square root of 4 is plus or minus 2.

questions.question: Which equation form is called slope intercept form?
options: x squared + y squared = r squared
questions.explanation: Slope intercept form is y equals mx plus b, where m is the slope and b is the y intercept.

questions.question: How many sides does a regular hexagon have?
questions.explanation: A hexagon by definition has six sides. Hex is the Greek prefix for six.

questions.question: What is the measure of each interior angle of an equilateral triangle?
questions.explanation: All three angles are equal and sum to 180 degrees, so each is 180 / 3 = 60 degrees.

questions.question: What is the length of the diagonal of a square with side length 4?
questions.explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem, diagonal = side x sqrt(2). 4 times sqrt(2) is the diagonal.

questions.question: What is 0.25 plus 1/4 expressed as a decimal?
Compute (3 + 4i)(3 - 4i).
questions.explanation: This is a difference of squares: 3 squared minus (4i) squared = 9 minus -16 = 9 + 16 = 25.

questions.question: If 2x + 3y = 12 and x = 3, what is y?
questions.explanation: Substitute x = 3: 2(3) + 3y = 12, so 6 + 3y = 12 and 3y = 6, giving y = 2.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
questions.explanation: The coulomb is the unit of electric charge. One coulomb equals one ampere flowing for one second.

questions.question: A short circuit is best described as which of the following?
options: A path of very low resistance
questions.answer: A path of very low resistance
questions.explanation: A short circuit allows current to flow with little or no resistance, often causing dangerously high current.

questions.question: Using P equals V squared divided by R, what is the power dissipated by a 5 ohm resistor with 10 volts across it?
questions.explanation: P equals V squared over R. 10 squared is 100, divided by 5 equals 20 watts.

questions.question: If voltage doubles across a fixed resistor, what happens to the current?
questions.explanation: By Ohm's Law, current equals voltage divided by resistance. With R fixed, doubling V doubles I.

questions.question: In a step down transformer, which side has more turns?
questions.explanation: Voltage scales with turns. A step down transformer has more primary turns and fewer secondary turns.

questions.question: How much current does a 100 watt light bulb draw at 120 volts?
questions.explanation: Current equals power divided by voltage. 100 / 120 is approximately 0.83 amperes.

questions.question: Which kind of materials have many free electrons?
questions.explanation: Conductors like copper have a sea of free electrons that allow current to flow easily.

questions.question: In a household US wiring system, what color is the neutral wire?
questions.explanation: By NEC convention, neutral wires are white or gray. Hot wires are typically black or red.

questions.question: In a US household wiring system, what color is the ground wire usually?
questions.explanation: Ground wires are colored green, green with yellow stripe, or left as bare copper.

questions.question: A device that converts AC to DC is called a what?
questions.explanation: Rectifiers (typically using diodes) convert alternating current to direct current.

questions.question: A device that converts DC to AC is called a what?
questions.explanation: An inverter takes DC input (e.g., from a battery) and outputs AC, often used in solar systems and UPS units.

questions.question: A fuse in a circuit is designed to do what?
options: Break the circuit if current is too high
questions.answer: Break the circuit if current is too high
questions.explanation: A fuse contains a wire that melts at a rated current, protecting downstream components from overcurrent.

questions.question: How many bits are in one byte?
questions.explanation: By definition, a byte is 8 bits. Half a byte (4 bits) is sometimes called a nibble.

questions.question: Which of the following are basic logic gates?
questions.explanation: AND, OR, and NOT are the three fundamental boolean logic gates. NAND, NOR, and XOR are common derived gates.

questions.question: A device that measures electrical resistance is called a what?
questions.explanation: Ohmmeters measure resistance in ohms. A multimeter combines voltmeter, ammeter, and ohmmeter.

questions.question: What is the standard unit symbol for capacitance?
questions.explanation: Capacitance is measured in farads, abbreviated F. C represents charge in coulombs.

questions.question: The speed of electric signals in a typical wire is closest to what?
options: About 50 to 90 percent of light speed
questions.answer: About 50 to 90 percent of light speed
questions.explanation: Signal propagation in a typical conductor is on the order of two thirds of the speed of light, depending on the medium.

questions.question: In a series circuit, the current at every point is what?
questions.explanation: Series circuits have only one path for current, so the same current flows through every component.

questions.question: What does AWG stand for in wire sizing?
questions.explanation: AWG is the standard US wire size scale. Higher AWG numbers correspond to thinner wires.

questions.question: Which AWG wire is physically thicker?
questions.explanation: Lower AWG numbers mean thicker wires. 12 AWG is thicker than 14, 20, or 22 AWG.

questions.question: A device that converts mechanical energy to electrical energy is called a what?
questions.explanation: Generators turn shaft rotation into electrical output. Motors do the inverse: electrical input becomes mechanical motion.

questions.question: What is the resistance of a circuit that draws 5 amps from a 120 volt source?
questions.explanation: By Ohm's Law, R equals V divided by I. 120 / 5 equals 24 ohms.

questions.question: An inductor opposes a change in what?
questions.explanation: Inductors store energy in a magnetic field and resist changes in current passing through them.

questions.question: A capacitor in a DC circuit at steady state behaves like what?
questions.explanation: Once fully charged in DC, no more current flows through a capacitor, so it acts like an open circuit.

questions.question: Which component is commonly used to protect a circuit by tripping when current is excessive but can be reset?
questions.explanation: A circuit breaker mechanically opens during overcurrent events and can be reset, unlike a fuse which must be replaced.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.explanation: Na comes from the Latin natrium. Sn is tin and S is sulfur.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for potassium?
questions.explanation: K is from the Latin word kalium. P is phosphorus and Pt is platinum.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for table salt?
questions.explanation: Common table salt is sodium chloride, NaCl, formed from sodium (Na) and chlorine (Cl).

questions.question: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Since 2006 the IAU classifies eight planets. Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet.

questions.question: What galaxy contains our solar system?
questions.explanation: Earth's solar system orbits the center of the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.question: The phase change directly from solid to gas is called what?
questions.explanation: Sublimation skips the liquid phase, as seen in dry ice (solid CO2) turning directly into gas.

questions.question: The phase change from gas to liquid is called what?
questions.explanation: Condensation occurs when gas molecules lose enough energy to become liquid, like dew forming on grass.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons. One newton accelerates a 1 kg mass at 1 meter per second squared.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of energy?
questions.explanation: Energy and work are both measured in joules. One joule equals one newton meter.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work. One watt equals one joule per second.

questions.question: What is the primary function of red blood cells?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin which binds oxygen and transports it to body tissues.

questions.question: What is the primary function of white blood cells?
questions.explanation: White blood cells (leukocytes) are the body's primary defense against pathogens and foreign material.

questions.question: How many teeth does a typical adult human have?
questions.explanation: A full adult set is 32 teeth, including four wisdom teeth, though many adults have wisdom teeth removed.

questions.question: The process by which water vapor escapes through the leaves of a plant is called what?
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water vapor through stomata in plant leaves. It helps draw water up from roots.

questions.question: Which atmospheric layer contains most of our weather?
questions.explanation: The troposphere is the lowest atmospheric layer and contains roughly 75 percent of the atmosphere's mass and almost all weather.

questions.question: Which atmospheric layer contains the ozone layer?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer sits within the stratosphere, roughly 15 to 35 km above Earth's surface.

questions.question: What is the most abundant element in the universe?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen makes up about 75 percent of the universe's normal matter by mass.

questions.question: What is the most abundant element in Earth's crust?
questions.explanation: By mass, oxygen makes up about 46 percent of Earth's crust, mostly bound in silicate minerals.

questions.question: Rocks formed from cooled magma or lava are classified as which type?
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form when molten rock (magma below the surface or lava above it) cools and solidifies.

questions.question: What element has atomic number 1?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen has one proton, making its atomic number 1. It is the lightest and most abundant element.

questions.question: What is the range of the pH scale?
questions.explanation: The standard pH scale runs from 0 (very acidic) to 14 (very basic), with 7 being neutral.

questions.question: What is the smallest structural and functional unit of life?
questions.explanation: All living organisms are made of one or more cells. The cell is the smallest unit considered alive.

questions.question: Plants make their own food through what process?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose, releasing oxygen as a byproduct.

questions.question: An animal with a backbone belongs to which group?
questions.explanation: Vertebrates have a spinal column made of vertebrae. Mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fish are vertebrates.

questions.question: Which gas do humans primarily exhale as a waste product of cellular respiration?
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration produces CO2 as a waste product, which is exhaled. We inhale oxygen and exhale carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Cordial most nearly means
questions.explanation: Cordial means warm and friendly, often used to describe greetings or relationships.

questions.question: Frugal most nearly means
questions.explanation: Frugal describes someone who is economical and avoids waste.

questions.question: Diligent most nearly means
questions.explanation: Diligent describes persistent, careful, and hardworking effort.

questions.question: Verify most nearly means
questions.explanation: To verify is to establish the truth or accuracy of something.

questions.question: Lucid most nearly means
questions.explanation: Lucid describes clear and easily understood expression or thought.

questions.question: Tedious most nearly means
questions.explanation: Tedious means tiresome and dull due to length or slowness.

questions.question: Apprehensive most nearly means
questions.explanation: Apprehensive describes a fearful or uneasy feeling about something to come.

questions.question: Concise most nearly means
questions.explanation: Concise means expressed clearly in few words.

questions.question: Augment most nearly means
questions.explanation: To augment is to make something greater by adding to it.

questions.question: Resilient most nearly means
questions.explanation: Resilient describes the ability to recover quickly from hardship.

questions.question: Obstinate most nearly means
questions.explanation: Obstinate describes someone who refuses to change their mind despite reason.

questions.question: Ambiguous most nearly means
questions.explanation: Ambiguous means open to multiple interpretations and lacking clarity.

questions.question: Candid most nearly means
questions.explanation: Candid means truthful and straightforward, even when uncomfortable.

questions.question: Meticulous most nearly means
questions.explanation: Meticulous describes paying very precise and careful attention to details.

questions.question: Reluctant most nearly means
questions.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling and hesitant to act.

questions.question: Tranquil most nearly means
questions.explanation: Tranquil means free from disturbance or peaceful.

questions.question: Adamant most nearly means
questions.explanation: Adamant means refusing to be persuaded or to change one's mind.

questions.question: Subtle most nearly means
questions.explanation: Subtle means so delicate or precise it is hard to detect.

questions.question: Defer most nearly means
questions.explanation: To defer is to put off or delay until a later time.

questions.question: Sparse most nearly means
questions.explanation: Sparse means thinly spread or scarce.

questions.question: Pertinent most nearly means
questions.explanation: Pertinent means directly related to the matter at hand.

questions.question: Coerce most nearly means
questions.explanation: To coerce is to persuade an unwilling person to do something through threat or pressure.

questions.question: The captain was steadfast in his decision. Steadfast most nearly means
questions.explanation: Steadfast describes someone who is firm and unchanging in commitment.

questions.question: The new soldier was vigilant during his watch. Vigilant most nearly means
questions.explanation: Vigilant means keeping careful watch for possible danger or difficulties.

questions.question: Robust most nearly means
questions.explanation: Robust means strong, healthy, and vigorous.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"Discipline is the foundation of military service. Without discipline, the most advanced weapons and the most talented soldiers cannot function as a unit. Drill, uniform standards, and chains of command exist to forge a group of individuals into a cohesive force."

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Weapons are more important than people
Discipline is essential for military effectiveness
Soldiers should be allowed to act independently
questions.answer: Discipline is essential for military effectiveness
questions.explanation: The passage repeatedly emphasizes that discipline transforms individuals into a cohesive force, making it the central idea.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"The Space Force was established as a separate service in 2019 to focus on space operations. Its mission includes protecting US assets in orbit, monitoring potential threats, and supporting joint operations. Guardians work with sophisticated satellite and cyber systems daily."

When was the Space Force established?
questions.explanation: The passage states the Space Force was established in 2019.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"Effective leaders communicate clearly. They explain not only what must be done, but why it matters. When subordinates understand the purpose behind an order, they execute with more initiative and judgment than if they were merely following instructions."

According to the passage, why should leaders explain the purpose of orders?
options: To take longer to give instructions
To improve initiative and judgment in subordinates
To reduce the number of orders given
questions.answer: To improve initiative and judgment in subordinates
questions.explanation: The passage states that understanding purpose improves how subordinates execute, citing initiative and judgment.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"Cybersecurity is no longer optional. Every organization, from small businesses to national defense agencies, depends on networks and data. A single compromised credential can lead to stolen secrets, financial loss, or operational disruption."

Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a consequence of compromised credentials?
questions.explanation: The passage lists stolen secrets, financial loss, and operational disruption, but not hardware damage.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"Physical fitness in the military is not vanity. It is operational readiness. A fit force endures hardship, recovers from injury faster, and performs longer under stress. Daily PT is an investment in mission capability."

What is the author's main argument?
options: Physical fitness directly supports mission performance
PT should be reduced to save time
questions.answer: Physical fitness directly supports mission performance
questions.explanation: The passage frames fitness as an investment in mission capability, making it the central argument.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"In the 1950s, integrated circuits were experimental. Today, billions of transistors fit on a chip the size of a fingernail. This exponential growth, often called Moore's Law, has driven the digital revolution."

What is Moore's Law described as in the passage?
options: An exponential growth pattern in chip transistor density
questions.answer: An exponential growth pattern in chip transistor density
questions.explanation: The passage describes Moore's Law as the exponential growth of transistors per chip.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"Pilots train extensively in simulators before flying actual aircraft. Simulators allow them to practice emergency procedures safely, repeating scenarios until responses become automatic. This reduces both training cost and the risk to lives and equipment."

Why are simulators valuable for pilot training?
options: They are faster than real flights
They allow safe practice that reduces cost and risk
questions.answer: They allow safe practice that reduces cost and risk
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that simulators reduce cost and risk while providing safe practice.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"Many cybersecurity breaches are caused not by sophisticated technical attacks, but by social engineering. An attacker might pretend to be IT support and ask for a password, or send a convincing phishing email. Training and skepticism are the best defenses."

According to the passage, what is the best defense against social engineering?
questions.explanation: The final sentence directly identifies training and skepticism as the best defenses.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"The submarine was first proven in combat during World War I, but its strategic role expanded in World War II. Modern nuclear submarines can stay submerged for months, making them a key element of nuclear deterrence."

Which conclusion is best supported by the passage?
options: Submarines were invented in World War II
Submarines today play a strategic deterrence role
Submarines no longer matter to navies
questions.answer: Submarines today play a strategic deterrence role
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says modern nuclear submarines are a key element of nuclear deterrence.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"Many young officers fear that asking questions makes them look weak. In fact, the most respected leaders ask the most questions. Leaders who pretend to know everything close themselves off from learning, and over time their judgment suffers."

What is the author's main point?
options: Asking questions strengthens, not weakens, leadership
Junior officers should know everything before promotion
Only senior officers should ask questions
questions.answer: Asking questions strengthens, not weakens, leadership
questions.explanation: The passage argues that questioning is a strength of effective leaders.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"Logistics is the unglamorous backbone of every campaign. Battles may be won by tactics, but wars are won by who can sustain forces in the field longer. Without fuel, food, and ammunition, the most skilled army grinds to a halt."

What is the author's central claim?
options: Tactics are more important than logistics
Logistics determines whether wars can be won
Soldiers do not need food in modern combat
Glamorous units are the most effective
questions.answer: Logistics determines whether wars can be won
questions.explanation: The passage argues that wars are won by sustainment, making logistics the deciding factor.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"Renewable energy sources, including solar and wind, now generate a significant share of electricity in many countries. Costs have fallen sharply over the past decade, making them competitive with fossil fuels in many markets."

Why have renewables become competitive with fossil fuels?
questions.explanation: The passage attributes the competitiveness specifically to falling costs over the past decade.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"Effective communication in any team requires more than speaking clearly. It also requires active listening. A leader who only broadcasts but never receives feedback will miss critical information from the people closest to the work."

What does the passage suggest about leaders who do not listen?
options: They miss critical information from those doing the work
questions.answer: They miss critical information from those doing the work
questions.explanation: The passage directly states that non listening leaders miss information from those closest to the work.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"GPS, originally designed for military navigation, now powers everything from smartphone maps to precision agriculture. The system relies on a constellation of satellites that broadcast precise time signals."

How does GPS work according to the passage?
options: Through ground based radio towers only
Via a constellation of satellites broadcasting precise time signals
questions.answer: Via a constellation of satellites broadcasting precise time signals
questions.explanation: The passage describes the GPS satellite constellation broadcasting precise time.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
"Every officer should learn to give clear written orders. A poorly worded directive causes delay, confusion, and sometimes mission failure. Clarity in writing is itself a force multiplier."

What can a poorly worded directive cause?
options: Delay, confusion, and possible mission failure
questions.answer: Delay, confusion, and possible mission failure
questions.explanation: The passage lists exactly these three consequences of poor directives.

questions.question: What is the primary function of an alternator in a vehicle?
options: Generate electrical power and charge the battery
questions.answer: Generate electrical power and charge the battery
questions.explanation: The alternator converts mechanical engine motion into electrical energy that powers the car and recharges the battery.

questions.question: What does a catalytic converter do?
questions.explanation: Catalytic converters use precious metals to convert harmful gases like CO and NOx into less toxic compounds.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of engine oil?
options: Lubricate moving parts and reduce friction
questions.answer: Lubricate moving parts and reduce friction
questions.explanation: Engine oil reduces wear by lubricating moving parts. It also helps cool and clean components.

questions.question: ABS stands for what in automotive terms?
questions.explanation: ABS prevents the wheels from locking up during hard braking, helping the driver maintain steering control.

questions.question: In a four stroke engine, what is the correct order of strokes?
questions.explanation: The four stroke cycle is Intake (air/fuel in), Compression, Power (combustion), Exhaust.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a spark plug?
questions.explanation: The spark plug delivers a high voltage spark that ignites the compressed air/fuel mixture in a gasoline engine.

questions.question: What does the transmission do in a vehicle?
options: Transfers engine power to the wheels at varying ratios
questions.answer: Transfers engine power to the wheels at varying ratios
questions.explanation: The transmission matches engine output to required wheel speed and torque through different gear ratios.

questions.question: What is the primary function of engine coolant?
questions.explanation: Coolant absorbs heat from the engine block and dissipates it through the radiator.

questions.question: What does a differential allow?
options: Wheels to turn at different speeds during turns
questions.answer: Wheels to turn at different speeds during turns
questions.explanation: The differential lets drive wheels rotate at different speeds, which is necessary when cornering.

questions.question: CVT stands for what?
questions.explanation: A CVT uses pulleys and a belt or chain to provide an infinite number of effective gear ratios.

questions.question: Which gauge typically measures engine RPM?
questions.explanation: The tachometer displays revolutions per minute of the crankshaft.

questions.question: What does the fuel injector do?
options: Sprays fuel into the intake or combustion chamber
questions.answer: Sprays fuel into the intake or combustion chamber
questions.explanation: Fuel injectors atomize fuel and deliver a precise spray into the engine for efficient combustion.

questions.question: The timing belt or chain synchronizes which two components?
questions.explanation: The timing belt keeps valve operation in sync with piston movement to prevent collision and maintain efficiency.

questions.question: Most car batteries are rated at what voltage?
questions.explanation: Standard automotive batteries supply 12 volts DC, made up of six cells of about 2 volts each.

questions.question: What does the crankshaft do?
options: Converts piston motion into rotational motion
questions.answer: Converts piston motion into rotational motion
questions.explanation: The crankshaft transforms the linear up and down motion of the pistons into rotation that drives the transmission.

questions.question: Compared to gasoline engines, diesel engines compress air to what?
questions.explanation: Diesel engines compress air much more, raising temperature high enough to ignite injected fuel without spark plugs.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the starter motor?
options: Spin the engine fast enough to begin running
questions.answer: Spin the engine fast enough to begin running
questions.explanation: The starter motor cranks the engine until combustion takes over and the engine runs on its own.

questions.question: ABS prevents what during hard braking?
questions.explanation: ABS pulses the brakes rapidly to keep the wheels rotating, preserving steering control.

questions.question: OBD II is a system used for what?
questions.explanation: OBD II is a standardized diagnostic system on US vehicles since 1996, used to read engine and emissions trouble codes.

questions.question: What does the air filter do?
options: Filter the air entering the engine
questions.answer: Filter the air entering the engine
questions.explanation: The air filter blocks dust and debris from reaching the engine, protecting cylinders and sensors.

questions.question: What is the function of the radiator?
questions.explanation: The radiator transfers heat from the engine coolant to the surrounding air via thin fins.

questions.question: Which component sends current to the spark plugs?
questions.explanation: The ignition coil steps up battery voltage to tens of thousands of volts to fire the spark plugs.

questions.question: FWD, RWD, and AWD describe what about a vehicle?
questions.explanation: These abbreviations describe whether the front, rear, or all wheels receive power from the engine.

questions.question: Why is tire rotation recommended periodically?
options: To even out tread wear and extend tire life
questions.answer: To even out tread wear and extend tire life
questions.explanation: Different positions on a vehicle wear tires differently, and rotation evens out the wear over time.

questions.question: Which fluid usually appears amber and is used in the braking system?
questions.explanation: Brake fluid is hydraulic fluid that transfers force from the brake pedal to the brake calipers.

questions.question: A claw hammer is primarily used for what?
questions.explanation: The flat face drives nails. The curved claw on the back pulls nails out.

questions.question: A Phillips screwdriver has what tip shape?
questions.explanation: Phillips heads have a cross or X-shaped recess. Flathead screws are slotted, and hex/Allen are hexagonal.

questions.question: A crescent wrench is also known as what?
questions.explanation: A crescent wrench has a movable jaw and is the most common type of adjustable wrench.

questions.question: What is the kerf of a saw?
options: The width of the cut the blade makes
questions.answer: The width of the cut the blade makes
questions.explanation: Kerf refers to the width of the slot a saw blade removes when cutting. Thinner kerf means less material loss.

questions.question: Plywood is typically made of what?
options: Layers of wood veneer glued together
questions.answer: Layers of wood veneer glued together
questions.explanation: Plywood is built from thin wood veneers (plies) glued with grain at alternating angles for strength.

questions.question: What does a miter saw specialize in?
questions.explanation: A miter saw is designed for accurate angled cuts, often 45 and 90 degrees, in trim and framing.

questions.question: With sandpaper, a higher grit number indicates what?
questions.explanation: Higher grit numbers mean smaller abrasive particles, producing a finer finish.

questions.question: A level is used to determine what?
options: Whether a surface is horizontal or vertical
questions.answer: Whether a surface is horizontal or vertical
questions.explanation: A bubble level uses a tube of liquid with a bubble that centers when the tool is level.

questions.question: A plumb bob hanging by a string is used to find what?
questions.explanation: A plumb bob uses gravity to indicate true vertical, used in framing and surveying.

questions.question: A chisel is used to do what to wood?
questions.explanation: A chisel is a sharpened blade tapped with a mallet to cut or shape wood, stone, or metal.

questions.question: A jigsaw is best suited for what type of cut?
questions.explanation: Jigsaws use a small reciprocating blade ideal for cutting curves and irregular shapes.

questions.question: On a circular saw blade, more teeth produces what?
questions.explanation: Higher tooth counts make finer cuts but feed slower; fewer teeth cut faster but rougher.

questions.question: A nominal 2x4 piece of lumber actually measures approximately what?
questions.explanation: Nominal sizes refer to rough cut. After drying and planing, a 2x4 measures roughly 1.5 by 3.5 inches.

questions.question: Pliers are most commonly used to do what?
questions.explanation: Pliers are gripping tools. Many include cutting jaws for wire.

questions.question: Vise grips are also called what?
questions.explanation: Vise grips clamp onto a workpiece and lock in place using an adjustable cam mechanism.

questions.question: A C clamp is primarily used to do what?
options: Hold pieces of material together while gluing or working
questions.answer: Hold pieces of material together while gluing or working
questions.explanation: C clamps press two surfaces together with a screw, often used during glue ups.

questions.question: A hacksaw is best for cutting what material?
questions.explanation: Hacksaws have fine, hard teeth designed to cut metal and plastics.

questions.question: An Allen wrench (hex key) is used for what?
questions.explanation: Allen wrenches drive screws and bolts that have a hexagonal recess.

questions.question: A torque wrench is used to do what?
questions.explanation: Torque wrenches measure rotational force, ensuring fasteners are tightened to a precise specification.

questions.question: Safety goggles primarily protect what?
options: Eyes from flying debris and chemicals
questions.answer: Eyes from flying debris and chemicals
questions.explanation: Goggles seal around the eyes to block particles, splashes, and impact debris.

questions.question: Which tool is best for stationary, precise drilling at consistent angles?
questions.explanation: A drill press is bench mounted, holding the bit perfectly perpendicular for accurate, repeatable drilling.

questions.question: PVA wood glue is what type of adhesive?
questions.explanation: PVA stands for polyvinyl acetate. It is a common water based wood glue that dries to a strong bond.

questions.question: A coping saw is best suited for what?
questions.explanation: A coping saw has a thin, replaceable blade in a frame, ideal for tight curves and detailed work.

questions.question: A nail gun is most commonly powered by what?
questions.explanation: Pneumatic and cordless battery powered nail guns are the two most common types in use today.

questions.question: A block plane is used to do what?
questions.explanation: A block plane uses a low angle blade to shave thin layers off wood for smoothing and fitting.

questions.question: A first class lever has the fulcrum positioned where?
options: Between the load and the effort
At the same point as the effort
questions.answer: Between the load and the effort
questions.explanation: First class levers (like a seesaw) have the fulcrum in the middle, with effort on one side and load on the other.

questions.question: A single fixed pulley provides a mechanical advantage of what?
questions.explanation: A single fixed pulley changes the direction of the force but does not multiply it. The MA is 1.

questions.question: In a block and tackle with 4 supporting rope sections, the mechanical advantage is what?
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage of a pulley system equals the number of rope sections supporting the load, which is 4 here.

questions.question: Two meshed gears rotate in which directions?
questions.explanation: When two external gears mesh, their teeth force each gear to rotate opposite to the other.

questions.question: If a small gear drives a larger gear, what happens?
questions.explanation: A small driver to a larger driven gear reduces output speed but multiplies torque.

questions.question: An inclined plane reduces what at the cost of increasing what?
questions.explanation: An inclined plane lets you lift a load using less force, but you must push it through a longer distance.

questions.question: A wedge is used to do what?
options: Split or hold materials by applying force at a narrow edge
questions.answer: Split or hold materials by applying force at a narrow edge
questions.explanation: A wedge converts force applied to its blunt end into outward force at its tapered edge.

questions.question: A screw can be thought of as which simple machine wrapped around a cylinder?
questions.explanation: Screw threads are inclined planes wound around a central shaft.

questions.question: Pascal's principle states that pressure applied to a confined fluid is what?
questions.explanation: Pascal's principle is the foundation of hydraulic systems. Pressure is transmitted unchanged through a confined fluid.

questions.question: Friction always acts in what direction?
options: Opposite to the direction of motion
questions.answer: Opposite to the direction of motion
questions.explanation: Friction is a resistive force that always opposes the relative motion or tendency of motion between surfaces.

questions.question: Static friction is generally what compared to kinetic friction?
questions.explanation: Static friction (which must be overcome to start motion) is typically larger than kinetic friction (during motion).

questions.question: Newton's third law states what?
options: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
questions.answer: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
questions.explanation: Newton's third law: forces always come in equal and opposite pairs between interacting bodies.

questions.question: Pressure is defined as what?
questions.explanation: Pressure equals the perpendicular force applied per unit area. Smaller area produces more pressure for a given force.

questions.question: Density is defined as what?
questions.explanation: Density equals mass divided by volume. Common units are kg/m^3 or g/cm^3.

questions.question: Work in physics equals what?
questions.explanation: Work is force applied over a distance in the direction of the force, measured in joules.

questions.question: If two forces of 10 N pull on an object in opposite directions, the net force is what?
questions.explanation: Equal and opposite forces cancel, producing a net force of zero.

questions.question: Acceleration is defined as what?
options: Change in velocity divided by time
Force divided by mass times time
questions.answer: Change in velocity divided by time
questions.explanation: Acceleration equals the rate of change of velocity. Note that F = ma is a separate consequence of Newton's 2nd law.

questions.question: Buoyant force on a submerged object equals what?
options: The weight of fluid the object displaces
questions.answer: The weight of fluid the object displaces
questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle: a body in a fluid is buoyed up by a force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces.

questions.question: A second class lever has what positioned between the fulcrum and the effort?
options: Nothing, they are at the same point
questions.explanation: In a second class lever (like a wheelbarrow), the load sits between the fulcrum and the effort.

questions.question: Power is defined as what?
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work, measured in watts (joules per second).

questions.question: If a driver gear has 20 teeth and a driven gear has 60 teeth, the gear ratio is what?
questions.explanation: Gear ratio compares teeth count from driver to driven. 20 to 60 simplifies to 1 to 3.

questions.question: Two equal weights are placed on a balanced beam. To stay balanced, the distances from the fulcrum must be what?
questions.explanation: For equal weights, equal lever arm lengths produce equal torques, keeping the beam balanced.

questions.question: Hydraulic systems amplify force because of what?
options: A small piston pushing fluid that moves a larger piston
questions.answer: A small piston pushing fluid that moves a larger piston
questions.explanation: By Pascal's principle, equal pressure on a larger area produces more force, multiplying the input force.

questions.question: Centripetal force on a body moving in a circle points where?
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is directed inward, perpendicular to motion, keeping the object in circular motion.

questions.question: Kinetic energy depends on which two quantities?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy equals one half mass times velocity squared. KE rises with both mass and (squared) speed.

questions.question: A square is rotated 90 degrees. What does the resulting shape look like compared to the original?
questions.explanation: A square has fourfold rotational symmetry. Rotating 90 degrees produces an identical square.

questions.question: How many faces does a cube have?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 square faces, 12 edges, and 8 vertices.

questions.question: Viewed directly from above, a cylinder appears as what shape?
questions.explanation: Looking down the axis of a cylinder, you see only the circular top face.

questions.question: Two parallel lines extended infinitely will do what?
questions.explanation: By definition, parallel lines remain a constant distance apart and do not intersect.

questions.question: Reflecting the point (3, 2) across the y axis gives what point?
questions.explanation: Reflecting across the y axis flips the sign of the x coordinate. The y coordinate is unchanged.

questions.question: Which 3D shape has 4 triangular faces and 1 square base?
questions.explanation: A square pyramid has a 4 sided square base and 4 triangular faces meeting at an apex.

questions.question: Two non parallel lines in the same plane will intersect at how many points?
questions.explanation: In a plane, any two lines that are not parallel must cross at exactly one point.

questions.question: A regular polygon has what property?
options: All sides and all angles equal
questions.answer: All sides and all angles equal
questions.explanation: Regular polygons are equilateral and equiangular. Examples include equilateral triangles and squares.

questions.question: Folding a square diagonally in half produces what shape?
questions.explanation: Folding a square along a diagonal creates two congruent right triangles.

questions.question: Two shapes are described as similar. What does that mean?
questions.explanation: Similar shapes have the same angles and proportional side lengths but may differ in scale.

questions.question: Which of the following is a 3D shape with two circular bases connected by a curved surface?
questions.explanation: A cylinder has two parallel circular bases and a single curved lateral surface.

questions.question: The shortest distance between two points is what?
questions.explanation: In Euclidean geometry, the straight line segment is the shortest path between two points.

questions.question: Translating a shape means moving it without changing what?
questions.explanation: Translation slides the shape across the plane while preserving its size, shape, and orientation.

questions.question: If a triangle has angles measuring 60, 60, and 60 degrees, what type is it?
questions.explanation: An equilateral triangle has three equal angles of 60 degrees and three equal sides.

questions.question: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
questions.explanation: A regular hexagon has 6 lines of symmetry, three through opposite vertices and three through opposite edge midpoints.
